statement: The two Pillar Two exemptions: the transitional CbCR safe harbour (Singapore s 20 and regs 69–74; Hong Kong Schedule 61 Part 3 Division 2 sections 2, 4, 6–8, 14) and the de minimis exclusion (Singapore s 19; Hong Kong Article 5.5). When qualified and elected by the filing entity, the jurisdiction's top-up amount for that year is zero (ss 19(4), 20(2); Article 5.5.1, Schedule 61 section 4), and no GloBE data of that jurisdiction is needed. Safe harbour: the financial year is within the transition period (with calendar-year financial years: years beginning in 2025 and 2026), the jurisdiction has a qualified CbC report, the safe harbour was applied in every earlier applicable year (once not applied it is lost for good: earlier years within the model follow the model result, years before that follow the group's statement), and one of three tests is met — de minimis (CbCR revenue < EUR 10 million and profit before tax < EUR 1 million or a loss), simplified ETR (simplified covered taxes ÷ profit before tax ≥ 16% (2025) / 17% (2026)), routine profits (profit before tax ≤ the substance-based income exclusion, or a loss). De minimis exclusion: three-year average revenue < EUR 10 million and three-year average GloBE income or loss < EUR 1 million, using the euro figures supplied by the group. Euro comparisons use the conversion rate supplied by the group (Singapore reg 9: the ECB average daily rate for December of the preceding calendar year; Hong Kong's conversion rule is in the OECD Commentary, not in the library). Neither Hong Kong nor Singapore has an eligible distribution tax system, so Singapore reg 70(1)(d) is met as a matter of course. Both elections are elections of the filing entity: ex ante a plan action (it can only lower the burden, and electing the safe harbour also keeps it available in later years), ex post a fact. Jurisdictional facts are recorded as group facts with a jurisdiction suffix (e.g. p2_cbcr_pbt_sg), and an answer does not travel with a role into another jurisdiction in a different candidate structure

statement: Reorganisation step: when the plan inserts a new HOLD between the existing ULT→OP (holding and repatriation templates), ULT transfers its OP shares to HOLD — one share transfer, recorded on the first modelled date and not repeated, whose consideration is data (if not given it must be asked: the income and the stamp duty both vary with it, unbounded), and each jurisdiction taxes it by its rules as usual. Mainland special tax treatment (财税〔2009〕59号 Articles 5, 7 and 8; 财税〔2014〕109号; 公告2013年第72号): a non-resident transferor → a non-resident transferee it holds 100% directly (Article 7(1)), Mainland tax deferred; the conditions are the five items of Article 5 (reasonable commercial purpose is a tax-authority determination; acquisition ratio ≥ 50% and equity payment ≥ 85% are plan design; no change of operations and no transfer within 12 months are plan commitments), unchanged withholding burden (yes when both parties are in the same place, otherwise a determination), the 3-year no-transfer commitment, and filing within 30 days (plan action); when HOLD later sells OP (or ULT sells HOLD) the Mainland tax basis carries over ULT's original tax basis (Article 6(2)), while the tax basis in other jurisdictions is the consideration; when the two parties are not in the same place, dividends HOLD receives that are paid out of pre-transfer profits get no treaty dividend relief (公告2013年第72号 Article 8; whether they are paid out of pre-transfer profits is a fact the plan can arrange). A resident transferor investing shares into a non-resident HOLD it holds 100% (Article 7(3), Article 8): the income is spread evenly over 10 tax years, and the share recognised within the period = years within the period ÷ 10; the treatment of a further transfer within the period is not provided for in the document and is not modelled. Relief under Hong Kong Stamp Duty Ordinance s 45 (associated bodies corporate, 90%) and Singapore Stamp Duties Act s 15 with the 2014 Rules (75% of voting capital and more than half the voting rights; a transferee newly set up specifically for the transfer is exempt from the 12-month association period): the application and remaining associated for 2 years are plan actions. HOLD's holding period in OP runs from the reorganisation, and the holding-period condition is a plan action (the reorganisation must be early enough), feasibility reviewed by a person. The step of redomiciling or dissolving the existing holding company is outside the model and marked "not counted" in the plan; when Hong Kong applies the intragroup transfer relief to the reorganisation step, the tax basis and acquisition date of a later sale carry over from the transferor (s 15OA(5), decision D44)

statement: Income inclusion rule (IIR): Hong Kong Schedule 60 Articles 2.1–2.3 (financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2025, s 26AE(6)), Singapore MEMTA Part 2 ss 11–15. Who applies it: the OECD transitional qualified status list names the IIRs of Hong Kong and Singapore (the Mainland is not listed); when the ultimate parent is in Hong Kong or Singapore it applies the rule; otherwise the intermediate parent in Hong Kong or Singapore applies it, unless a controlling parent above it applies a qualified IIR (Articles 2.1.2, 2.1.3, s 13(2)); a partially owned parent (more than 20% held outside the group) applies it itself, unless wholly owned by another partially owned parent that applies it (Articles 2.1.4, 2.1.5, s 13(3)). On whom: only members outside the parent's own jurisdiction (Article 2.1.6, s 11(2)); Hong Kong and Singapore members have a qualified domestic top-up tax and apply its safe harbour, so their IIR top-up amount is zero (Article 5.2.3, second table of the list), hence v1 computes it only for Mainland members. How: the Mainland jurisdiction is computed in aggregate under the rules of the parent's jurisdiction (effective tax rate, substance exclusion, transitional safe harbour and de minimis exclusion, additional current top-up amount) and allocated to members by positive income; the parent's share = member share × inclusion ratio (ownership chain, Article 2.2.2), less the part already charged on a lower parent applying the IIR (Article 2.3, s 14(2)); the pseudo-flow iir:<member>><parent> is paid by the parent itself and recorded in its jurisdiction. UTPR: Hong Kong awaits a date appointed by notice in the Gazette (s 26AE(7)), no such notice is in the library, not modelled; Singapore has no UTPR. The domestic top-up tax does not push down CFC tax (Schedule 62 section 6 removes Articles 4.3.2(c), (d)), consistent with the original model

statement: Flow facts on the side of a newly set up company: the flow facts written in the case describe the parties in the client's existing structure. When one party in a candidate is a company newly set up by the plan (new HOLD, IPCO_NEW, SERVICER_NEW etc.), the facts the case wrote for that party's side are not carried over — on the payer side: whether taxed abroad, tax rate, headline rate, whether traded on a listed market, whether the payer can deduct, whether the underlying profits are taxed and their tax share; on the payee side: whether the income is received in its jurisdiction, whether held as trading stock, R&D expenditure, whether the IP was never held by a Hong Kong business, whether the lender's interest is chargeable in Hong Kong, the profit margin on service fees; a share transfer is further split into buyer, seller and target sides. What the law can settle, the law settles (the statutory rate of the new company's jurisdiction is its headline rate); what the plan controls is designed (the new company is unlisted, ordinary dividends are not deductible, whether income is remitted is set by the plan; a new IP company that buys the IP has no R&D of its own, so its R&D fraction is zero, Schedule 17FC section 5(3)(c)); the rest is asked separately at the address "flow~company-jurisdiction", and the answer is used for that candidate only without changing the facts of the client's existing companies. statement: IP transfer step: when the company holding the IP in a candidate is not the current holder, the new holder buys the IP ownership from the current holder (iptx) at the price the case gives (market value on the transfer date, must be asked if not given), recorded on the first modelled date and not repeated; the current holder stays in the graph (the proceeds stay in that company, what happens to them afterwards is outside the template). The seller is a non-resident: Implementing Regulations Article 7 does not list intangible assets as a source rule and item (6) is to be determined by the competent departments, which has not been seen, so it is a tax-authority determination, and if determined to be domestic, 10% withholding (Law Article 19(2)); Article 13(7) of the Arrangement and Article 13(6) of the China–Singapore treaty leave other property gains to the seller's residence jurisdiction (residence certificate required, no Mainland permanent establishment, principal purpose test still applies). The buyer amortises in the Mainland on a straight line over not less than 10 years or the shorter period set by law or contract (Article 67), counting only the modelled years. VAT: a foreign seller's IP is consumed in the Mainland, 6% withheld by the buyer, creditable for a general taxpayer holding the contract, payment proof and the statement or invoice; a domestic seller is taxed at 6% wherever the buyer is; a technology transfer is exempt when recognised by the provincial science and technology or industry and information technology department (plan action; whether a foreign seller with no "place of location" can obtain recognition is a tax-authority determination); the zero rate (Implementing Regulations Article 9(2)) requires use entirely abroad, and in this template OP keeps using it in the Mainland, so it does not apply. Stamp duty: instrument of property transfer at 0.03%, paid by each party; when both parties are abroad it depends on whether the instrument is used in the Mainland (e.g. registering the Mainland patent or trademark assignment). Hong Kong: a non-resident selling to a Hong Kong buyer does not carry on business in Hong Kong, not charged; a buyer purchasing from an associate gets no deduction (s 16EC(2)). A Hong Kong seller: proceeds in excess of the undeducted expenditure, capped at the deductions obtained, are Hong Kong-sourced trading receipts (ss 16E(3), 16EB(2)); offshore gains received in Hong Kong are IP disposal gains (s 15I, deemed non-capital), and qualifying IP (patents, software copyright) is exempted by the R&D fraction (Schedule 17FC); when Hong Kong-sourced it is chargeable only if non-capital; source and capital nature are tax-authority determinations. Singapore: an outright purchase is not a payment for "use or the right to use" (s 12(7)), no withholding; the buyer claims writing-down allowances over the elected minimum of 5 years (s 19B(1AA), (1AB)), none for acquisitions after the end of the basis period for YA 2028 (s 19B(10)(aa)), none where a related seller obtained a deduction in Singapore for creating the IP (s 19B(10A), presumed no for a foreign seller). A Singapore seller: proceeds in excess of the allowances not yet granted, capped at allowances granted, are taxable (s 19B(4), (5)), the rest is capital unless determined otherwise (s 10(1)); IP of a resident owner is situated in Singapore and s 10L does not apply (s 10L(15)(k)); a newly set up Singapore company makes only zero-rated supplies, recovers input tax in full and the reverse charge does not apply (design). statement: When interest, royalties or service fees paid by a related party to the payee are below the arm's-length amount (arms_length_value: comparable uncontrolled price, or the median of the comparable range), the payee's jurisdiction computes revenue at the arm's-length amount. The Mainland under Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 41 adjusts amounts below the median to the median under 公告2017年第6号 Article 25 paragraph 3 and charges interest on the payee's additional tax (Article 44, depending on whether the payee provided contemporaneous documentation); Hong Kong under s 50AAF(1) does not adjust a price within the arm's-length range (at or above arms_length_low) (DIPN 59 paragraph 121) and outside the range usually adjusts to the median (paragraph 122); Singapore under s 34D(1A)(a) adjusts into the range (IRAS guidance 5.115) and charges 5% on the increase under s 34E(1)(a) (guidance 9.2: whether or not tax is payable). The adjustment is a multiplier on the amount, multiplied with the income and profit share, not a second tax base (the check of decision D32 excludes it). No adjustment without a given arm's-length amount, and like the payer's deduction cap (arms_length_max) it rests on the case's transfer pricing documentation. Corresponding adjustment in the payer's jurisdiction: Article 9(2) of the Arrangement, Article 9(2) of the treaty (replaced through Article 17(1) of the Multilateral Instrument), Hong Kong s 50AAN; the "appropriate adjustment" is decided by the payer's competent authority, in the model a determination (granted at the lower bound, not at the upper), and a result written in the case (corresponding_adjustment_granted) is followed; there is no treaty between Hong Kong and Singapore and so no corresponding adjustment. Singapore s 10L(10): when a foreign asset is sold below open market price and the gain is received in Singapore, the Comptroller may treat A + B − C as the gain received; in the model remittance means the whole gain, so the gain share is (open market price − tax basis) ÷ sale price; whether it applies is a determination, and a case stating it (s10l_open_market_applied) is followed; a zero price means no gain received (e-Tax Guide 11.3). Partial remittance (the 10,000 of K2.SGL17) is outside the model. Not covered: assessment of the VAT base (VAT Law Article 20), Hong Kong adjustments of s 15(1)(b) royalty income of non-residents, remission of the Singapore surcharge.

statement: Trade in goods (trading template: OP manufactures and sells to customers outside the group directly, or resells through a group trading company placed by the plan). The seller is taxed on its gross margin: price (for a related buyer paying less, the arm's-length price, decision D41) less cost of goods sold (the manufacturer's production cost; the trading company's purchase price), and the trading company's resale further deducts its own expenses (operating_costs, asked for a new company). A trading company buying from a related supplier: what it pays above the upper limit of the arm's-length range is costed at the upper limit by its jurisdiction; when the supplier's jurisdiction taxes the supplier at the arm's-length price, the trading company's jurisdiction may make a corresponding adjustment (treaty Article 9(2), determination). The buyer's purchase is not a separate deduction item but goes into the cost of its resale; a new trading company's after-tax profit and GloBE income are resale less purchase price less own expenses. Source: the Mainland taxes a non-resident seller only on Mainland-sourced income (Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 3(3)), and income from the sale of goods is sourced where the transaction takes place (Implementing Regulations Article 7); a business agent who habitually concludes contracts or stores and delivers goods on its behalf constitutes an establishment (Article 5), so with an establishment in the Mainland whether the income is Mainland-sourced is a determination, at 25%; without one, its sales to a Mainland buyer are completed abroad and not taxed. Hong Kong: trading profits are sourced where the purchase and sale contracts are effected (DIPN 21 paragraph 23) — both in Hong Kong, fully taxable; both outside, not taxable; only one in Hong Kong, presumed taxable subject to all the operations (determination); the profits are either wholly taxable or wholly not (paragraph 24); selling to a Hong Kong customer or buying from a Hong Kong supplier is presumed to be a contract effected in Hong Kong; where a new trading company's contracts are effected is a plan action (by its staff travelling or by an overseas agent, paragraph 25). The manufacturer's own sales: the source of the profits is a determination (s 14). Singapore: trade income under s 10(1)(a), whether the trade is carried on in Singapore is a determination, foreign-sourced income taxed when remitted. A non-resident seller with no fixed place in Hong Kong or Singapore does not carry on business there and is not taxed. Over several years each year's resale matches that year's purchases.

statement: Turnover taxes and customs duty on goods crossing borders. Route: the delivery place delivered_to is given by the case; the dispatch place defaults to the manufacturer's jurisdiction (in the template OP produces where it is located), and for a resale to the dispatch place of its purchase; a trading company that does not handle the goods has the purchase shipped straight to the customer (routed_via_trader, a plan action for a new company), while a trading company in the same place as the goods buys locally and declares the export itself. Mainland export: VAT zero rate (VAT Law Article 10(4)), input tax refunded at the refund rate, which is the applicable rate unless the Ministry of Finance and STA provide otherwise (公告2026年第11号 Article 3; the goods' refund rate is case data), and the shortfall of the refund rate below the applicable rate goes into export cost (Article 5(3)): the manufacturer on the FOB price (exempt-credit-refund, Article 4(1)), a foreign trade enterprise on the special invoice amount of its purchase (exempt-refund, Article 4(7)). When the rate is not given the lower bound counts nothing and the upper bound takes the highest goods rate of 13% with no refund. Export duty is paid by the consignor (seller) at the tariff rate. Mainland import: the duty taxpayer is the consignee (Tariff Law Article 3), the buyer in the model; ad valorem (Article 23), the dutiable value based on the transaction price plus freight and insurance up to the place of entry (Article 24), and when buyer and seller have a special relationship and the price is below arm's length, whether the relationship affected the price is a determination; import VAT is the dutiable value plus duty times the applicable rate (VAT Law Article 14), credited as input tax by a general taxpayer (Article 16). When a group company exports or imports and the tariff rate is not given, it is a mandatory question. Consumption tax, bonded materials under processing trade and the offset for duty-free raw materials are outside the model. Singapore: GST on imported goods (s 16), paid by the importer (buyer), no cost when input tax is fully recoverable; the provisions on Singapore's zero-rated exports and goods outside Singapore not being taxed could not be brought into the library (SSO blocked), so the model sets no GST item on goods sales by a Singapore seller; Singapore customs duty on dutiable goods such as liquor, tobacco, motor vehicles and petroleum is outside the model. Hong Kong has no VAT and no duty on general goods, no item. Flows before the respective VAT and tariff laws took effect are outside the library (decision D30).

A capitalisation is a dividend flow the payer records as share capital (capitalised), sourced from retained earnings (surplus reserve, undistributed profits) or from capital reserve formed by share premium (capitalised_from; capitalising other capital reserve is outside the model). Mainland: capitalising retained earnings is recognised as dividend income of the investor on the date of the capitalisation decision (国税函〔2010〕79号 Article 4 paragraph 1; annual return A107011 columns 6 and 7) and follows the dividend rules; capitalising share premium is not dividend income and does not increase the tax basis (Article 4 paragraph 2), for domestic and foreign investees alike. The investor's tax basis: no provision says outright that capitalising retained earnings increases the tax basis, so it is fixed at an increase by the capitalised amount on this chain of evidence — Article 4 paragraph 1 recognises dividend income; paragraph 2 denies both income and tax basis only for premium capitalisation; a foreign investor "adding or capitalising" paid-in capital with distributed profits is direct investment with distributed profits (财税〔2018〕102号 Article 2(1)1, 公告2025年第2号 Article 2(2)1), 公告2017年第37号 Article 3 takes the "contribution cost actually paid" as the tax basis, and Implementing Regulations Article 56 takes the expenditure actually incurred on acquisition as historical cost; Mainland only, the cost in other jurisdictions is still the amount actually paid. For a foreign investor, a Mainland company's capitalisation is a reinvestment within the payer itself, the funds passing through no other account (财税〔2018〕102号 Article 2(3)), and when the conditions are met withholding tax is deferred. Stamp duty: business books at 0.025% of the increase in the aggregate of paid-in capital (share capital) and capital reserve (Stamp Duty Law Article 5(3), Article 11, table of items and rates); capitalising retained earnings increases that aggregate (财政部 税务总局公告2024年第14号 Article 1(4)), capitalising premium leaves it unchanged. Hong Kong and Singapore: a capitalisation pays nothing and is not received locally under s 15H(5) and s 10(25); IRD Advance Ruling Case No. 75 also found a dividend in specie of shares of a foreign company not received in Hong Kong. End of the reinvestment deferral: when the investor recovers the investment by transfer, buy-back or liquidation, the tax is paid within 7 days of receipt (财税〔2018〕102号 Article 6); the model's sale and liquidation dispose of the whole holding, the deferred part is disposed of first (公告2018年第53号 Article 11), and the deferral ends in full; a partial capital reduction needs the capital accounts to apportion and is asked instead; when the investee is not given and the investor disposes of a Mainland company in the flow, reinvested_into is asked; the late-payment surcharge on the recovered tax runs from that deadline, and when the general anti-avoidance rule denies the deferral it still runs from the payment date (财税〔2018〕102号 Article 4). Before this the model's deferral never ended: withholding tax was understated when the holder exited after deferral. The holding template may capitalise OP's retained earnings to the holder before the exit (Event.capitalisable, structure variable capitalise).

statement: Branches. A company's branch in another jurisdiction is not a separate person: the case writes branch_profit_<j> (the branch's profit for the year) and branch_period_end_<j> (the end of that year, defaulting to the date of the last flow in the modelled year) on the head office, the engine places the branch as a BRANCH entity in that jurisdiction and a BRANCH_PROFIT flow to the head office. The branch's jurisdiction taxes on its own computation: the Mainland taxes a foreign enterprise's establishment at 25% on its income (Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 3(2), Article 4), no withholding (Article 37 reaches only Article 3(3) income); Hong Kong taxes only profits sourced in Hong Kong (s 14, determination); Singapore taxes trade income from a trade carried on in Singapore (s 10(1)(a), determination, as in decision D42). The head office's jurisdiction: a Mainland resident enterprise's foreign branch income is included whether or not repatriated, in the Chinese year in which the foreign tax year ends (财税〔2009〕125号 Article 3(1), Article 11), with credit for the tax paid abroad (Article 23); a loss does not offset domestic profit (Article 17), the model places no flow, and loss carry-forward (Operating Guide Example 2) is outside the model. A Singapore company's foreign branch profit is taxed when received in Singapore (branch_receipt_<j>), exempt when the s 13(9) conditions are met (s 13(8)(b); taxed locally branch_taxed_<j>, presumed yes by law for a Mainland branch), otherwise credited. A Hong Kong company's foreign branch profit is taxed only if sourced in Hong Kong (s 14), and FSIE does not include business profits (s 15H). Schedule 54 Part 2 section 2(1): Hong Kong's unilateral credit applies only to specified foreign-sourced income chargeable under s 15I(1); before this the model also gave unilateral credit for Singapore-sourced service fees and goods profits, corrected (hk.ftc.unilateral covers only FSIE income and IP disposal gains). Scope: a Hong Kong MNE entity includes a stand-alone entity with a permanent establishment in another jurisdiction, and a group with a member or permanent establishment outside the ultimate parent entity's jurisdiction is an MNE group (s 15H(1)); the relevant group of Singapore s 10L needs more than one entity, with the members not all in one jurisdiction or any member having a place of business in more than one jurisdiction (s 10L(5)(b)) — a single company with a foreign branch is not a group (e-Tax Guide paragraphs 5.5, 5.6). A permanent establishment is taken from the branch or fixed_place_in_<j>, asked when unknown and decisive. Not covered: other flows received or paid by a branch (triangular cases applying the treaty by the head office's residence), internal payments between head office and branch (Implementing Regulations Article 49), Pillar Two treating a permanent establishment as a constituent entity, the branch-versus-subsidiary choice template.

New income type PROPERTY_TRANSFER (sale of land use rights or buildings), sourced where the property is located (Implementing Regulations Article 7(3); property_loc). Mainland: VAT 9% (VAT Law Article 10(2)); for property acquired before 30 April 2016 a general taxpayer may elect the simplified method at 5% in 2026–2027, and if not self-built the sales amount is the tax-inclusive price less the original purchase price (公告2026年第10号 III(2)4, 5, IV(8)), a small-scale taxpayer at 3% on the same difference (Article 11); a general-taxpayer buyer credits input tax on the invoice. Land appreciation tax: revenue net of VAT, deducting the appraised price of the old building (including the land price, lat_appraised_value) or the purchase invoice uplifted 5% per year (one year per full 12 months, a remainder over 6 months beyond a year counts as a year) plus the deed tax on purchase, plus the urban maintenance and construction tax, local education surcharge and stamp duty on the transfer; four-bracket progressive rates on the appreciation ratio with quick deductions (Regulations Articles 4–7; Rules Articles 7, 10; 财税〔2006〕21号 Article 2; 国税函〔2010〕220号 Article 7; 公告2016年第70号; 公告2026年第3号 Article 5); sales by real estate developers are outside the model. Deed tax 3%–5% set by the province (deed_tax_rate, both ends when not given), on the transaction price net of VAT, borne by the buyer (Deed Tax Law Articles 1, 3, 4; 财税〔2016〕43号). Stamp duty: instrument of property transfer at 0.05%, each party. Income tax: a non-resident at 10% on proceeds less net value of the property (Article 19(2)), with no deduction of the taxes on the transfer; a resident enterprise on the price net of VAT less tax basis and the taxes on the transfer (Implementing Regulations Article 31). Hong Kong: ad valorem stamp duty on Hong Kong immovable property at Scale 1 (Cap 117 First Schedule head 1(1), the band rates with marginal relief), all parties liable, allocated by contract (stamp_borne_by, must be asked if not given); the gain is chargeable under s 14, capital asset a determination; a Hong Kong company selling foreign immovable property: a non-IP disposal gain accrued and received from 2024 falls under FSIE (Schedule 56), exempt on economic substance; a trader's gain from its business is not specified foreign-sourced income and is taxed only if the profit is sourced in Hong Kong (determination). statement: Losses. A company's income tax in its jurisdiction is computed on the taxable income of the year: the revenue and deductions of the flows, other taxable income written in the case (taxable_income_other, per year or the same each year, may be negative) and losses brought forward from earlier years (loss_brought_forward, [year, amount(, type code)]). Each flow is added year by year (the difference with and without the flow): a change in the year's figure alters the year's entries proportionally (a loss absorbs revenue, absence of income absorbs deductions), and the effect on later years or on another group company is recorded as the entry's carry (a tax amount, not credited). Mainland: domestic income and foreign income by country are kept apart (Article 17; 财税〔2009〕125号 Article 3(5)); domestic losses carry forward five years, A106000 types 200, 300 and 400 ten years, types 500 and 600 for 2020 losses eight years, earliest expiring first; whether foreign income offsets domestic losses is the enterprise's election (A100000 line 23), which reduces that country's limit accordingly, and when the limit is zero the foreign tax carries forward (Operating Guide ¶27, Example 8), ex ante the lower-tax option under the single objective, ex post asked if not written; a foreign branch loss offsets only income of the same country, and the non-actual part has no time limit (¶14, Example 2). Hong Kong: set off in the year, the balance carried forward indefinitely (s 19C(4)); when a change in shareholding has the sole or dominant purpose of using the losses, they may not be set off against profits after the change (s 61B, determination). Singapore: losses carried forward, earliest first, no time limit (s 37(3)(a), (5)); not deductible when the shareholders are not substantially the same (50%, looking through companies), and after a ministerial waiver only against the same trade (s 37(12)–(17)); group relief (s 37B): 75% ownership between Singapore-incorporated companies (multiplied through Singapore companies), the year's unabsorbed loss transferred to a company with chargeable income in proportion to days in the group, elected by both, ex ante the lower-tax option. When the case writes no other income, has no losses and no flow creates a loss: the marginal model as before (cit_rate); when a flow creates a loss and other income is unknown: ask, the lower bound treats it as absorbed, the upper bound as not. Pillar Two: the use and creation of losses carry deferred tax, recast at the minimum rate (GloBE Article 4.4.1), and covered taxes at the lower of the two rates when the loss stage was untouched; losses transferred out under group relief carry no deferred tax.
